findings: Professional US equity historical bid/ask collection required the complete Network A, B, and C Level 1 set; the NYSE Global Index Feed did not satisfy NYSE stock requests.
New market-data entitlements did not reach the API client until Trader Workstation was fully restarted.
Per-candidate raw caching converted repeated entitlement retries into resumable work and preserved 21 early successes, then 49 final successes, without recollection.
A retired SEMR contract produced IBKR error 200 after the final universe was frozen; resolving its archived contract moved it to VALUE, where IBKR exposed no historical minute data.
A legitimate zero-range LOB opening bar exposed a validator mismatch: real flat OHLC is valid input but remains an ineligible non-bullish setup.
follow_ups: Build a provider-neutral valuable-data cache with provenance, versioning, integrity hashes, retention policy, and privacy classification.
Evaluate the pre-freeze gate on the next historical candidate pool and measure avoided collection time and blocked-batch rate.
impact: Historical candidate pools now preflight symbol contracts before the final ten names are frozen, allowing retired names to be replaced from a ranked buffer without observing target-session prices.
Provider-wide permission and connection failures remain hard blockers instead of being misclassified as bad symbols.
Flat opening bars reach the strategy's existing bullish-candle rejection instead of aborting bundle construction.
Future meaningful engineering outcomes are captured by an audited append-only history and enforced at commit time.
summary: The first frozen five-day replay pass resolved market-data entitlements and exposed the boundary between resumable collection failures, retired-symbol fidelity blockers, and valid flat market bars.
title: First five-day replay hardened the historical data path

findings: The January 6 replay date had only five verified earnings events across the holiday lookback, while the SEC EDGAR daily 8-K/6-K feed provided a complete pre-price catalyst universe.
historical_bundle_builder.py previously required surprise_rank and EPS fields for every candidate even though the strategy permits issuer, SEC, exchange, analyst, and other material catalysts.
follow_ups: Resume the cached 10-day collection after TWS login and keep sparse quote/lookback failures as explicit date blockers.
impact: Historical collections can freeze and audit non-earnings primary catalysts while existing earnings bundles retain their prior discovery schema.
summary: A randomly selected low-earnings date exposed an earnings-only bundle-builder assumption; the builder now preserves validated generic point-in-time discovery records without changing strategy gates.
title: Generalized historical discovery evidence

findings: March 12 and April 23 produced complete validation-grade bundles from the frozen universes.
January 26 NKSH returned only 13 of 14 required opening-volume observations; January 6 ODYS and March 4-5 THO contained invalid opening-volume lookbacks.
February 3 FUBO, February 18 DMC, and March 31 KEEL lacked required historical top-of-book ticks, while June 18 ODTX had no IBKR historical trade bars.
Re-running the exact selection failed before context or ledger writes because eight selected dates lacked valid bundles.
follow_ups: Choose explicitly between stopping historical mode and starting a new independently seeded batch; do not substitute dates or candidates into this failed manifest.
impact: The workflow preserved the unbiased frozen sample and treated sparse provider history as a blocker rather than replacing candidates after observing target-session data.
Successful raw responses and the two valid bundles remain cached locally for reproducible follow-up without contaminating the public signal ledger.
summary: A seed-frozen ten-date batch completed point-in-time universe and market-data collection without broker actions, but only two dates met the full bundle contract; the exact selection guard prevented partial replay publication.
title: Frozen ten-day replay exposed persistent IBKR fidelity gaps

findings: All-or-nothing run_selected_dates discarded two validation-grade dates whenever any selected bundle was missing.
A TWS disconnect was previously caught inside the symbol loop, producing false failures for every remaining symbol instead of terminating and reconnecting.

Three selected histories had nonpositive or incomplete OR_RVOL lookbacks and four lacked point-in-time quote/trade evidence; these are provider-fidelity failures, not permission to weaken the 14-positive-session live rule.

Rejected candidates can have negative raw resistance room and reward/risk; the evaluator needs those values for explanation, while the nonnegative public ledger correctly represents no upside room as zero.
A copied 63-bit random seed lost integer precision in an evidence manifest even though the authoritative selection JSON remained exact.
follow_ups: Configure and entitlement-test the Massive SIP fallback, then run a fresh 20-date random batch and require at least 16 validation-grade dates with zero substitutions and cascade errors.
Keep the production OR_RVOL input rule unchanged until a separately approved versioned strategy review earns a different semantic contract.
impact: Ready-only mode replayed March 12 and April 23 into 22 audited public records while preserving the other eight exact selected dates as blockers and making zero substitutions.
The collector now stops each blocked date at its first permanent failure, reconnects once on retryable transport interruption, and resumes from per-provider caches.
Pre-freeze history checks and an optional provider-neutral Massive SIP fallback move failures earlier or recover missing primary data without inspecting target outcomes.
Public batch status preserves exact selection integrity, typed failure reasons, replay progress, and the fixed 20-date/80-percent engineering gate.
summary: The ten-date failure showed that batch atomicity, transport cascades, sparse primary-provider data, metric serialization, and seed precision were independent infrastructure blockers; the repaired workflow completed both valid dates without substitutions.
title: Ready-only replay restored historical evidence throughput

findings: The old 45-day five-minute probe was split into seven provider chunks per symbol and repeated opening and daily history during bundle collection.
A symbol-scoped SPTX HMDS no-data error aborted the old transaction after roughly 24 minutes and discarded partial progress.
The optimized cold pass examined 102 symbol-date entries in 736.5 seconds and the exact cached rerun completed in 1.13 seconds.
SPTX passed when the probe stopped requesting unnecessary older history; GALT and NUVL were safely skipped from frozen buffers.
follow_ups: Measure cold and cached throughput on a new 20-date acceptance batch and address Massive fallback authorization.
impact: Interrupted and repeated historical preflights resume per symbol and date instead of restarting.
Bundle collection reuses no-lookahead pre-session history and eliminates duplicate opening and daily requests.
Symbol-specific missing history remains skippable while pacing, permission, connection, timeout, and provider-wide failures remain hard blockers.
summary: A 24-minute preflight failure exposed duplicate immutable requests and missing checkpoints; versioned cache, adaptive windows, and reuse made the exact batch resumable and faster.
title: Resumable preflight cache accelerated historical batches

findings: The first ten archived replays contain 100 rejected candidates and no performance-bearing signals; 60 candidates failed immutable pre-session ADV or ATR gates, so target-session collection for those names was avoidable.

Ninety candidates carried a chase rejection, and schema-1 bundle construction used quotes from the start of the same minute whose later high established the breakout, creating a point-in-time mismatch.

The historical adapter requested opening history before cheaper daily eligibility checks and used a small five-minute chunk plan even though the current IBKR duration table permits the required 28-day window in one request.
follow_ups: Benchmark the new daily-first preflight on a fresh cold 20-date batch and record provider request counts, elapsed time, cache reuse, and validation-grade yield.
Collect new schema-2 replay evidence before drawing any strategy-performance conclusion.
impact: Preflight now rejects known non-common-stock, dilution-conflicted, low-ADV, and low-ATR candidates before target-session work, then uses one 28-day opening-history request only for survivors.
Rule-qualified pre-session caches and frozen manifests bind reusable history with content hashes so altered or stale-rule inputs fail closed.
Schema-2 bundles reserve a full post-break minute for quote observation and evaluate at its closing boundary, while legacy schema-1 bundles remain readable and immutable.
The production strategy remains frozen and UNVALIDATED because the reviewed sample has no eligible or closed performance signals.
summary: A full code and evidence review moved known pre-session rejects ahead of expensive data pulls and corrected a replay timestamp defect without changing production strategy rules.
title: Historical preflight and replay fidelity hardened

findings: A 53-name Monday pre-open earnings, material-event, and executive-change draft exhausted at only eight symbols meeting the immutable ADV and ATR gates.
Extending the same frozen date to the permitted March 27 after-16:00 ET SEC 8-K window added WMT and HE, producing ten viable symbols from a 77-name ranked buffer.
The final preflight skipped 50 names, left 17 unused buffer names, observed no target-session prices, and the completed bundle replayed with zero substitutions or cascade errors.
follow_ups: Measure viable-name yield and buffer depth across the next newly randomized batch before changing the default buffer target.
impact: Future historical discovery should cover both the previous-session after-close and current-session pre-open catalyst windows before the first preflight.
A deep ranked buffer lets strict liquidity and ATR gates reject aggressively without weakening fidelity or substituting after target data is observed.
summary: The March 30 replay needed the complete prior-session after-close catalyst window to freeze ten viable names without looking at target-session prices.
title: After-close catalyst buffer rescued a sparse replay date

findings: The March 30 preflight used 54 cold IBKR-backed symbol records totaling 87.943 symbol-seconds and the target-session raw capture spanned 49.362 seconds, while exact cache reuse was approximately one second.

The old preflight graph issued 118 calls because all 54 provider-backed names received contract lookup and daily history even though 44 failed immutable ADV or ATR gates; moving explicit lookup behind those gates reduces the same graph to 74 calls.

A four-worker 118-call live trial took 123.34 seconds and a subsequent two-worker 74-call trial inside the same load window took 121.68 seconds, confirming that IBKR soft throttling can erase naive concurrency gains and that uncoordinated processes would be unsafe.
follow_ups: Run the independently requested 100-day timed historical batch, then repeat its exact frozen inputs from cache and compare stage-level wall time, request counts, cache reuse, validation-grade yield, substitutions, and cascade errors.
impact: Preflight and bundle collection now share one bounded ordered scheduler, so slow responses can overlap without changing frozen rank order, date order, substitution rules, or the first-failure boundary.

The read-only adapter reserves globally spaced send times, caps in-flight requests, classifies message-rate failure as retryable, and emits per-kind request, pacing, concurrency, cache, and wall-time telemetry.
summary: The one-day trace showed that cold IBKR request shape and soft throttling, not evaluation CPU or local JSON, dominate replay latency; the collector now eliminates rejected-name lookups, overlaps a bounded request window deterministically, and reports the evidence needed to tune large runs.
title: Bounded collection exposed request-count and provider-throttle bottlenecks

findings: An all-market SEC join fanned out to thousands of registrants that immutable ADV and ATR gates would reject, so the strategy-specific discovery lane now starts from high-market-cap earnings and direct material filings.
A 40-name reserve produced too few viable candidates on early dates; the frozen selection was retained and the reserve was expanded to 80 before continuing.
SEC exchange mapping alone does not prove the broker contract is common stock; accepted preflight rows now require IBKR stockType COMMON and older cache entries are invalidated.
follow_ups: Screen primary documents incrementally until each date has enough clean reserve names, and add an interval-aware per-symbol market-data cache to reduce repeated IBKR history requests across nearby dates.
impact: Historical discovery now emits point-in-time, dilution-screened, no-target-price draft manifests from resumable cached sources instead of requiring manual date-by-date research.
Large preflights can record one exhausted date and continue later frozen dates with zero substitutions, while provider-wide failures still stop the stream.
summary: The timed 100-day run replaced manual per-date catalyst research with cached earnings and SEC discovery, expanded ranked reserves after an early yield check, and made sparse dates independent without weakening replay gates.
title: Automated discovery made large historical batches fail-soft

findings: HBANZ repeatedly timed out as the first uncached historical-bars request while the same SEC registrant had already contributed HBAN and several other secondary tickers.
Fresh connections and a 180-second timeout reproduced the same first-symbol stall, distinguishing a bad discovery row from a general TWS outage.
follow_ups: If representative-symbol ambiguity appears for true multi-class common issuers, add point-in-time security-type metadata rather than restoring every instrument.
impact: Discovery now ranks one deterministic shortest ticker per SEC CIK, preventing preferred and depositary siblings from consuming ranks or historical requests.
The resumed January 22 preflight reached ten candidates and advanced normally; IBKR stockType COMMON remains the final eligibility proof.
summary: A repeated HMDS timeout was traced to a secondary ticker emitted beside its registrant common ticker; discovery now freezes one representative issuer symbol before broker proof.
title: Issuer deduplication removed a historical farm stall

findings: The end-to-end frozen workflow took 19,681.079 seconds; preflight alone submitted 4,612 IBKR requests and spent 3,673.363 seconds waiting on pacing, while the main bundle segment took 3,779.680 seconds.

A stale-cache refresh and evaluator-safe reject boundary recovered 11 dates in 139.058 seconds, leaving only five dates with genuinely missing historical bid/ask ticks and producing 95% yield with zero substitutions or cascade errors.
Exact warm preflight used 3,040 cache hits and zero provider requests in 0.704 seconds; a clean local run evaluated 950 signals across 95 days in 13.328 seconds, or 7.13 days per second.
follow_ups: Add interval-coverage and single-flight storage so nearby cold dates can reuse larger historical ranges before evaluating a bulk research-data provider for corpus expansion.
impact: Historical research now uses one bounded shared IBKR session for cold acquisition and immutable local artifacts for repeated strategy evaluation.
Incompatible ignored raw caches refresh once, zero-volume or non-break candidates become safe hard rejects, and optional fallback failures cannot reconnect the healthy primary lane.
The public batch, archived contexts, signal ledger, and machine-readable speed report retain the 100 original dates, seed, blockers, timings, and provider telemetry.
summary: The frozen 100-day historical speed test reached 95 validation-grade replays and proved that IBKR acquisition and pacing dominate while exact cached research runs complete in seconds.
title: One-hundred-day run isolated cold acquisition from fast replay

findings: The first audit found four schema-valid date bundles whose ordered symbols did not match the current public evidence manifest; date and schema validation alone were insufficient cache identity.

Rebuilding all 95 evidence-bound bundles reused 926 candidate raws, collected 36 missing candidates with 92 IBKR requests, and took 201.790 seconds; five genuine quote-boundary dates remained blocked with zero substitutions and cascade errors.

The final four-strategy matrix completed 400 date-strategy evaluations in 2.003 seconds with four processes versus 7.332 seconds serially, made zero provider calls, and produced identical stable results.

Opening reversal led the exploratory matrix at +14.879R and 1.320 profit factor, ORB was modestly positive, high-of-day continuation was near flat, and the tested VWAP pullback was negative; none is promotion evidence without independent confirmation.
follow_ups: Freeze the opening-reversal specification before collecting independent confirmation dates, and redesign or reject the current VWAP-pullback definition rather than tuning it on this sample.
impact: New bundles carry and verify a frozen-evidence content hash, while research replay independently requires exact ordered candidate equality before using a date.

Versioned plugins receive progressively revealed immutable prefixes, enter only on the next bar, share one conservative execution model, and write isolated ignored shards plus compact public comparisons.
summary: A process-parallel research plane now reuses immutable daily bundles for several versioned strategies without provider or production-ledger writes, while an identity audit repaired four stale same-date bundles that belonged to older frozen universes.
title: Evidence-bound bundles enabled fast isolated strategy matrices

findings: The cached four-strategy 100-day matrix completed in 2.003 seconds with zero provider calls, while the cold end-to-end corpus took 19,681.079 seconds.
Contract lookup was secondary: 990 requests accumulated 29.161 provider-seconds versus 14,020.172 provider-seconds for 3,622 historical-bar requests.
The unfinished 500-day pass retained useful per-symbol/date checkpoints, and an SEC market-holiday master index absence needed official quarter-index confirmation rather than repeated retries.
follow_ups: Use the existing 95-day corpus for rapid hypothesis work and collect new dates only for missing coverage or independent confirmation.
Evaluate an entitled bulk daily/minute/quote provider for corpus expansion because IBKR historical bars remain the dominant cold-path cost.
impact: Learning mode now runs a versioned eight-phase inspect, adversarial-filter, one-slice apply, validate, record, and stop workflow with no broker or automatic strategy authority.
IBKR contract proofs are request-qualified, integrity-checked, expiring, atomic, single-flight, and reusable across dates; provider-wide failures are never cached.
SEC holiday index gaps become verified cached empty inputs, while malformed quarter listings and listed-but-unavailable daily indexes still fail closed.
summary: The 500-day attempt and 100-day telemetry showed that learning should iterate over the frozen local corpus in seconds while historical-bar acquisition expands independently; a bounded mode and cross-date contract cache now encode that priority.
title: Bounded learning mode separated fast iteration from cold acquisition

findings: The current production gate stack selected zero trades, while the same immutable corpus contained 90 bar-executable ORB counterfactuals; rejected-signal outcomes are necessary to measure alpha gates.

Only simple early reversal strength and the Item 2.02 earnings subset passed positive retrospective phases, a positive one-sided 90% bootstrap lower bound, all target tests, and PF/drawdown gates at 10 and 20 bps per side.

The preferred earnings reversal produced 67 trades, +21.110R, PF 1.683, and 4.528R maximum drawdown; at 20 bps per side it retained +9.813R and PF 1.282, but this inspected corpus is not independent evidence.

Its median 2.088% structural stop and 11.4% risk-implied median notional are incompatible with the current 0.8% stop cap and aggressive allocation objective; tightening the stop destroyed the ORB variant.
follow_ups: Freeze at least 100 newly uninspected dates under the published early-earnings-reversal confirmation contract; require at least 80 usable dates and 50 trades without substitution.
Collect subminute NBBO and protection evidence and resolve the structural-stop versus risk-sized-notional deployment geometry before any cadence-qualified production proposal.
impact: The complete 15-policy, 240-cell policy/cost/target matrix reused 95 evidence-bound bundles in 14.003 seconds with zero provider calls and byte-identical production artifacts.
The work prunes tight-stop ORB and VWAP pullback, deprioritizes HOD continuation, and rejects complex score/RVOL reversal selectors after severe-cost failure.
Exact frozen scanner/candidate hashes, ordered universes, source attestations, bundle hashes, deterministic implementation identities, and blocked dates make future comparisons auditable.
summary: A frozen-corpus counterfactual matrix showed that the zero-trade production stack cannot learn from closed outcomes, isolated two early reversal confirmation candidates, and kept production rules frozen.
title: Production-aware lab restored trade-capable learning labels

findings: The first implementation reparsed strategy_config.toml 3,800 times; an isolated benchmark measured 3,800 load_config calls at about 1.12 seconds.
Policy evaluation also resolved the same immutable plugin for every observation even though each policy uses one strategy identity.
The optimized final run retained dataset hash 651f20ff135eecf850292066b5c75652cddb85914a2b30e707f12c3b84df9d3d, the same two confirmation candidates, and zero production or provider writes.
follow_ups: Keep cold historical-bar acquisition separate from repeated local policy evaluation; the former remains the dominant end-to-end bottleneck.
impact: The 240-cell lab completed in 12.055 seconds, 13.9% faster than the initial complete 14.003-second pass.
Immutable configuration and plugin reuse shortens every local learning iteration without weakening point-in-time or production-isolation checks.
summary: Loading production configuration and strategy plugins once per run reduced the complete local counterfactual matrix from 14.003 to 12.055 seconds without changing evidence or policy results.
title: Immutable run inputs shortened the strategy lab

findings: Independent confirmation must freeze the complete new date and ordered Item 2.02 universe before target-session collection; an implementation or source timestamp alone cannot prevent post-outcome substitution.

The promising reversal's structural stop and the production 0.8% cap are different hypotheses: risk-sized account deployment can preserve invalidation without forcing the 70% allocation objective, while a naturally tight cohort must remain separate.

Minute-bar expectancy cannot establish signal observation, fresh executable NBBO, chase-cap fills, or prompt protection, so those fields now have a prospective hash-sealed shadow lifecycle rather than being inferred from historical next-open prices.
follow_ups: In a separately selected historical workflow, freeze and collect at least 100 uninspected dates with at least 80 validation-grade dates and 50 signals; stop without tuning if any predeclared gate fails.
After an independent historical pass, collect at least 20 completed no-order shadow signals across at least 30 calendar days before normal cadence review.
impact: Hash-addressed preregistration rejects inspected-date overlap, manifest or implementation drift, pre-registration capture, phase relabeling, symbol reorder, and substitution while executing only the frozen early Item 2.02 reversal.
Confirmation results now separate R expectancy from whole-share structural-stop account compounding, log growth, drawdown, allocation shortfall, stop slippage, and a non-compressed <=0.8% cohort.

The prospective shadow runner has no account or order-action interface and records no-trade, missed, invalid, stop-first ambiguous, target, and force-flat lifecycles with quote and protection timing gates.
summary: The early earnings reversal now has an isolated fail-closed qualification plane that separates independent expectancy, safe structural deployment, and prospective execution evidence without changing production rules or exposing an order path.
title: Preregistered confirmation and no-order shadow evidence close the reversal gap

findings: The hash-addressed manifest bce91ee770205ee7b6c25e976fb70547f64fe6fdbde16ae1722c3cbf400f627a froze the exact 100-date seed 1003109952991718283 with zero overlap against strategy-lab-651f20ff135e-b268f18ec755; two exhausted candidate universes remained explicit pre-collection blockers instead of being substituted.

Post-registration collection produced 31 validation-grade confirmation bundles and 19 target-data blockers before the twenty-first total missing date made the required 80-date minimum impossible; the remaining 48 dates were left untouched and the stage stopped without threshold tuning.

The sole frozen early Item 2.02 reversal policy produced 22 trades, -10.056R, -0.457R mean expectancy, 0.370 profit factor, and 10.492R maximum drawdown at 5 bps per side and 2R; every target and cost-stress cell was negative.

Risk-sized structural-stop deployment compounded -2.298% with zero risk-cap violations or stop compression; only six naturally occurring stops were at or below 0.8%, which was insufficient for cohort inference and also negative.
follow_ups: Reject or redesign the early Item 2.02 reversal on genuinely new evidence; do not advance it to shadow execution qualification or tune it against this confirmation sample.
impact: Confirmation manifests now retain exact requested dates and ordered partial universes when preflight exhausts, and the collector binds confirmation bundles to the preregistration hash with capture timestamps after registration.
The failed confirmation is public and auditable while strategy_config.toml, production ledgers, maturity, trade contexts, and broker state remain unchanged.
summary: The preregistered 100-date independent confirmation stopped at its evidence gate and the observed subset decisively failed the frozen performance thresholds, so the early Item 2.02 reversal will not advance.

findings: Ryan delegated every in-scope operational, research, engineering, and trading judgment to Codex, including choices that would ordinarily pause for extra safety checks or confirmation.
Clear requests now map directly to a session mode; ambiguous requests use the most useful non-expansive mode, and missing historical day counts are chosen proportionately then frozen exactly.

Evidence-qualified strategy application decisions no longer wait for routine approval, but hard risk caps, evidence gates, broker constraints, login or MFA, and tool-mandated direct confirmation remain authoritative.
impact: Codex must decide, document material rationale, run useful checks automatically, and continue instead of turning compliant in-scope choices into permission prompts.
Every delegated decision is governed by the objective of explosive but stable geometric account growth after execution costs and operational risk.
summary: Repository governance now treats Ryan's in-scope decision authority as delegated to Codex while preserving irreducible platform and authority boundaries.
title: Decision authority delegated to the trading agent

findings: Public append-only dataset, experiment, and strategy registries now preserve negative results and evidence suitability across bounded agent invocations.
The resumable controller hashes protected production artifacts, performs atomic state transitions under a single-run lock, and stops at explicit judgment or evidence boundaries.
The failed early Item 2.02 reversal is seeded as retired evidence and cannot silently return as an unregistered threshold variant.
follow_ups: Add daily account simulation and selection-aware statistical controls.
Add point-in-time security identity and scanner-faithful dataset lanes.

The controller exposes no broker or production-activation path and fails if protected strategy or public trading artifacts change during a run.

title: Persistent registries and resumable learning state established

findings: Every requested trading day now produces an account return; missed, rejected, and no-signal outcomes remain explicit zeros instead of disappearing from the denominator.
Dependence-aware stationary bootstrap, Deflated Sharpe, PBO, Holm family correction, and power targets account for temporal dependence and repeated strategy searches.
Signal intent, detection, order intent, fill outcome, protection state, costs, and account compounding remain separate fields.
follow_ups: Feed registered experiment families through the statistical contract.
Use scanner-faithful daily universes before making production ORB claims.
impact: Higher modeled execution cost cannot improve a strategy by deleting a bad fill, and no-trade coverage is reflected in geometric growth.
Promotion-facing results disclose the size of the searched family and use corrected evidence rather than an isolated retrospective Sharpe ratio.
summary: The learning plane now evaluates daily geometric account outcomes with dependence and strategy-selection controls instead of IID trade-only summaries.
title: Daily account paths and selection-aware statistics implemented

A production replay contract must bind scanner rules and security-master hashes and reconstruct a dynamic complete 09:35 ET universe from then-available information.
Point-in-time symbol intervals preserve renamed, retired, and delisted identities; current symbol resolution cannot substitute for a failed historical listing.
